stdout:
Build kit for "button"

Start from the TEMPLATE, fill it with BLOCKS, and use COMPONENTS only for what is left.
Changing a page you already have? Keep it, and use only the blocks and components.

TEMPLATE
The idea is a part of a page and names no page, so it starts from the app shell. Scaffold it, then put blocks inside it.

name:        shell-top-nav
package:     @astryxdesign/core
displayName: Top Nav
description: Application frame with horizontal navigation only: a centered bar whose items open full-width mega-menu panels, over placeholder content that keeps the entire width.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template shell-top-nav --type page <path>

Install missing dependencies: npm install @heroicons/react@"^2.2.0"

This template uses StyleX. Your project needs a StyleX compiler plugin - see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs styling-overview` for setup steps.

BLOCKS
Ready-made sections for parts the template lacks. Print one: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template <name>

name:        ButtonWithIcon
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      template
displayName: Button - Icon
score:       90
reason:      keyword "Button"
description: Buttons with a leading icon that reinforces the label. Use when the icon helps the user identify the action faster, like a plus for "New" or a trash can for "Delete".
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template ButtonWithIcon --type block

name:        ButtonVariants
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      template
displayName: Button - Variants
score:       90
reason:      keyword "Button"
description: All 4 button variants in default, disabled, and loading states. Use primary for the main action, secondary for most others, ghost for low-emphasis, and destructive for dangerous actions.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template ButtonVariants --type block

name:        ButtonShowcase
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      template
displayName: Button - Variants
score:       90
reason:      keyword "Button"
description: All four button variants side by side: primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive. A quick visual reference for choosing the right variant.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template ButtonShowcase --type block

name:        ButtonFloating
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      template
displayName: Button - Floating
score:       90
reason:      keyword "Button"
description: A floating action button raised with `elevation="med"`. Use elevation for buttons that hover above content, like a FAB.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template ButtonFloating --type block

name:        ButtonWithEndSlot
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      template
displayName: Button - End Slot
score:       90
reason:      keyword "Button"
description: Buttons with a trailing badge showing a count or status. Use for notification counts, unread messages, or any button that needs a visual indicator.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template ButtonWithEndSlot --type block

COMPONENTS
For what the template and blocks do not cover. Read one: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component <name>

name:        IconButton
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      component
score:       90
reason:      keyword "button"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/IconButton
description: A button that shows only an icon with no visible text. Use IconButton in toolbars, table rows, and compact UI where space is tight and the icon is universally understood.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component IconButton

name:        useClickableContainer
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      hook
score:       90
reason:      keyword "button"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useClickableContainer

name:        useInteractiveRole
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      hook
score:       90
reason:      keyword "button"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInteractiveRole

name:        ButtonGroup
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      component
score:       88
reason:      keyword "buttons"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/ButtonGroup
description: ButtonGroup joins related actions into a single connected control. Use it when multiple buttons represent related choices or operations that belong together visually, like copy/cut/paste, or undo/redo.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component ButtonGroup

name:        NavIcon
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      component
score:       70
reason:      keyword "nav button"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/NavIcon
description: NavIcon is a circular icon container with an accent-colored background. Use it in navigation headers such as TopNavHeading and PageNavHeader to visually identify a section or application.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component NavIcon

name:        SegmentedControl
package:     @astryxdesign/core
domain:      component
score:       70
reason:      keyword "button-group"
import:      @astryxdesign/core/SegmentedControl
description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, dragging the selected segment carries the selection along with the selected label's colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go (letting go outside the control selects nothing); a tap selects through the browser's click; a pressed segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing lifts or dims. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme's duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component SegmentedControl
